extracted.intended_audience: military lawyers, judge advocate staff, state military and government officials responsible for militia administration
extracted.subtask_description: Compilation of legal standards and administrative rules governing the Organized Militia/National Guard: calling forth, organization, training, property, funds, pay, and related duties under federal statutes and War Department/Attorney General holdings. Covers when militia may be federalized, composition and organization requirements, and responsibilities for property/funds/transportation/inspections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Calling forth — lawful purposes
rubrics_metrics.description: The power to call forth the Organized Militia is restricted to the objects mentioned in section 8, article 1, of the Constitution: 'to execute the laws of the Union, suppress insurrection, and repel invasion.' There is no power to call forth the militia in anticipation of war.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Held that the President cannot call forth the Organized Militia for garrisoning posts beyond continental U.S. in anticipation of war; use outside U.S. only when conditions would warrant calling forth under the Constitution. (C. 16273, June 1904; cns. cited.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Calling forth — manner and channels
rubrics_metrics.description: The calling out of the militia by the President may be made through the governor of the State or to any militia officer he deems proper; Congress/acts indicate forms (including historical conscription).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The act of May 27, 1908, provides it is lawful for the President to issue orders through governors or commanding generals of militia of D.C.; if governor refuses, President may address orders directly to proper organization commanders. (C. 4003, Nov. 3, 1910.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Calling forth — effect on members
rubrics_metrics.description: Members of an organization called forth shall be compelled to enter the service of the United States; calling forth removes the force from the status of 'militia' under certain statutes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Held that calling forth compels entry into U.S. service and removes militia status as used in §1661, R.S. (C. 14148, Mar. 1906 and Mar. 1908; C. 5455, Dec. 19, 1898.)

rubrics_metrics.name: President as sole judge of necessity
rubrics_metrics.description: The President is the sole judge of the necessity for calling forth the militia and his judgment is conclusive on others.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Held repeatedly (e.g., Martin v. Mott) and cited in opinions (C. 14148, Dec. 29, 1911).

rubrics_metrics.name: Militia vs. Federal troops — status during joint encampments
rubrics_metrics.description: Participation in joint encampments with the Regular Army does not, by itself, place militia into the service of the United States unless they were 'called forth' as prescribed by the Constitution and statute.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If not properly called forth, militia remain State forces; injuries during such participation are claims against the State, not War Department; U.S. not responsible for loss/damage (C. 14971; C. 16925; C. 20402).

rubrics_metrics.name: Militia members not federal employees for certain offenses
rubrics_metrics.description: Members of the Organized Militia are not 'in the service of the United States' for purposes of statutes punishing sale/purchase of arms/etc. by persons employed in U.S. military service (secs. 3748 and 5438, R.S.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Held that these sections do not apply to Organized Militia members. (C. 14148-E, Mar. 23, 1908.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Organization must conform to Regular/Volunteer Army
rubrics_metrics.description: Within five years from Jan. 21, 1903, the organization of the Organized Militia shall be the same as that prescribed for the Regular and Volunteer Armies (subject to Secretary of War exceptions in time of peace).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Until the five years expire, a State's authorized Organized Militia is the force in existence Jan. 21, 1903; changes within five years must conform or extra officers won't be recognized for federal allotments/payments. (C. 14148 holdings.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Organizational structure specifics (infantry, cavalry, artillery)
rubrics_metrics.description: Infantry: companies → battalions (4 companies) → regiments (3 battalions). Cavalry: troops → squadrons (4 troops) → regiments (3 squadrons). Field artillery: batteries → battalions (3 batteries) → regiments (2 battalions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If Organized Militia includes those branches, it must be organized into the corresponding unit types to qualify for annual federal allotments under §1661. Establishment of higher commands than regiments committed to State discretion. (C. 14148-B, F.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Machine-gun platoon rule
rubrics_metrics.description: A State is not required to create a machine-gun platoon if none existed; but if it has one, its organization must conform to that of the Regular Army as fixed in War Department orders/regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Machine-gun platoon is not essential to Regular Army battalion/regiment, so absence does not violate conformity requirement; if provided, must match Regular Army form. (C. 14148-G, June 28, 1907.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Coast artillery and enlisted ratings
rubrics_metrics.description: Ratings prescribed by acts for Coast Artillery of Regular Army apply to Coast Artillery troops of Organized Militia in operation of sections 14 and 15 of Jan. 21, 1903 act as amended.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Statutory ratings fully applicable. (G. 14148-H, July 1, 1910.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Discrimination on basis of color
rubrics_metrics.description: If a State discriminates in composition of its Organized Militia because of color, the federal militia act deprives the Federal Government of power to devise or apply an adequate remedy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Held that discrimination prevents federal remedy under the act. (G. 14148-B, Mar. 10, 1906.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Militia office not civil office
rubrics_metrics.description: Office in the militia is not a civil office; Regular Army officers are not prevented by civil-office restrictions (e.g., §1222, R.S.) from accepting militia commissions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Thus Regular Army officers may accept militia commissions. (G. 29273, Dec. 2, 1911.)

rubrics_metrics.name: State cannot create forces exempt from calling forth
rubrics_metrics.description: A State cannot create a force which shall be exempt from being called forth by the President; such creation would contravene constitutional restrictions on State powers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Held in multiple opinions that forces intended to be exempt are unlawful. (C. 14148, Sept. 5, 1903; Aug. 10, 1908.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Unauthorized/voluntary organizations not militia
rubrics_metrics.description: Purely voluntary organizations, cadet corps of boys under 18, insular police, Alaska Indians, or other bodies lacking statutory militia status are not entitled to militia benefits or appropriations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: Fremont Signal Corps not entitled to stores (C. 14148-O); cadet corps at universities not part of Organized Militia (C. 14148-D); insular police of Puerto Rico not entitled (C. 11604).

rubrics_metrics.name: Enlistment qualifications
rubrics_metrics.description: There are statutory qualifications for enlistment in the militia (able-bodied men between ages 18 and 45, and specific state requirements).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A cadet company of boys under 18 cannot be considered militia and cannot receive benefits under §14 of Jan. 21, 1903. (C. 14148-A, Dec. 2, 1905.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Instruction — theoretical and field training rules
rubrics_metrics.description: The Organized Militia may receive theoretical instruction at Regular Army schools and by details from the Regular Army (officers/enlisted men), and field instruction via state camps, with detailed rules on participation, selection of location, subsistence stores, disbursing officer duties, reimbursements, and limitation of allowances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific items: governors select participation and place; instruction may be given on military reservations with permission; subsistence stores may be sold; disbursing officers not entitled to commutation of quarters in camp; reimbursement rules for transportation, damage to crops, foundered horses, etc.; no fund for entertainment of attaches; many cited holdings. (Sections VI.A–B and joint camps rules.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Target practice range acquisition and use
rubrics_metrics.description: Acquisition of ranges may be by setting aside public land, purchase, or lease, with rules on lease execution, sufficient description, insurance, equipment (water plant), forage issue, and that U.S. will not protect use of range.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lease may be for several years; insufficient description with actual occupation discussed; damage to leased property, renting ranges as pasture, and selection of damage boards under guidance. (Sections VI.C and holdings.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Transportation responsibilities and entitlements
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules cover freight, storage, drayage of equipment for ranges; transport of new material to militia and return of old to U.S.; freight from state arsenals to company stations; transportation of target teams; land-grant reductions for travel under War Dept orders.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When traveling under War Dept orders entitled to 50% land-grant reduction same as regular troops in some cases; specific holdings determine applicability for en route to joint encampments. (Militia VII items.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Armory provision and restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: States have a duty to provide armory facilities; armories may not be used for drill purposes by aliens.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State's duty affirmed; aliens restricted from using armories for drill. (Militia VIII.)

rubrics_metrics.name: United States property — issuance, loans, accountability
rubrics_metrics.description: U.S. property issues (books, clothing, equipment), sales to a State require request by governor, loans of property to militia not authorized, governor accountable, rules for repair, recovery of property from men, disposition of condemned clothing, and surveying officer affidavit requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Act references (May 27, 1908) and numerous holdings: loan of property to militia not authorized (C. 728), loan to D.C. Guard by Sec. of War not authorized in general (various holdings); surveying officer requires affidavits (page citations).

rubrics_metrics.name: United States funds — disbursement and inspection
rubrics_metrics.description: How U.S. militia funds are disbursed: sec. 1667 R.S. remain available until expended; funds may be turned over to State on governor's request and disbursed under his direction; inspection of disbursing officer's accounts required; clerk for disbursing officer not allowed; certain territories treated for allotment purposes; veterinary care and caretaker pay rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific holdings: Hawaii held to be a Territory for allotment; caretaker for U.S. property cannot be paid from federal funds; inspection procedures for disbursing officer accounts. (Militia X items.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Pay — who and what is payable
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules on pay of adjutants general, heads of staff departments at state camps, officers authorized for pay at joint encampments, pay of disbursing officers, assistant surgeons; extra pay items (keeping horse), longevity pay, pay of officers on special duty preparing camp ground, pay of members of damaged property boards, pay of deceased soldier claims, and other enumerated entitlements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Many specific holdings on eligibility and computation of pay; e.g., allotments under §1661 cannot be used to reimburse state losses in some cases (C. 20402). (Militia XI items.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Small arms, ammunition, and equipment — exchange and issue
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules for exchange of new for old arms and issuance of ammunition to militia forces.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific references to exchange programs and issue procedures; see Militia XII entries (A: exchange of new for old; B: issue of ammunition).

rubrics_metrics.name: Uniforms and insignia control
rubrics_metrics.description: Federal control over uniforms, including campaign badge rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Uniform regulation and campaign badge addressed in Militia XIII entries; National Guard of D.C. uniform matters elaborated. (Militia XIII.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Official correspondence and use of penalty envelopes/telegrams
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules for correspondence including the use of penalty envelopes and telegrams in official militia/quartermaster/disbursing correspondence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quartermaster's agents designated for transportation may use penalty envelopes in official correspondence (G. 14148-F, July 1908). (Militia XIV.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Canteen at state maneuver campgrounds
rubrics_metrics.description: Regulation regarding canteens at state maneuver camp grounds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Canteen treated as a distinct administrative item with restrictions; see Militia XV.

rubrics_metrics.name: National Guard of District of Columbia — definition and administration
rubrics_metrics.description: Definitions, disbandment, retiring board, retirement, service of government employees in the Guard, uniform, property responsibility, evidential value of officer certificates, supplies and statutory references, loan of property restrictions, and discharge of enlisted men.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific statutory acts and holdings cited (acts of March 1, 1889; March 2, 1903; loan of property not authorized, etc.). (Militia XVI sections.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Volunteers — examination for volunteer commissions
rubrics_metrics.description: Examinations are required to determine classes of men eligible for volunteer commissions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedural rules and standards for examinations referenced under Militia XVII A.

rubrics_metrics.name: Naval militia rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Provisions for the Naval Militia of the States and of the District of Columbia, with applicable qualifications and administration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See Militia XVIII A–B for scope and applicability (page citations).

rubrics_metrics.name: Naturalization — militia service not counting
rubrics_metrics.description: Service in the militia does not count toward naturalization of an alien.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Held explicitly that militia service does not count toward naturalization requirements. (Militia XIX A.)

rubrics_metrics.name: History and legislative acts concerning regiments
rubrics_metrics.description: Historical statutory references (e.g., Act of March 2, 1895) relevant to regimental history and legal status.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used for background and interpretation; cited under Militia XX.

rubrics_metrics.name: Opinions not rendered by Judge Advocate General on purely state matters
rubrics_metrics.description: The JAG will not render opinions on militia questions that relate only to the State (i.e., matters outside federal jurisdiction).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guides the scope of federal legal advisory actions. (Militia XXI.)
